key_insight: The paper demonstrates deterministic, site-selective direct writing of individual perovskite quantum dots with <25 nm placement control and single-atomic-scale resolution for quantum light emission.
engineering_relevance: This enables practical integration of high-purity single-photon emitters into photonic devices, overcoming the stochastic placement problem that has limited perovskite-based quantum and optoelectronic architectures.
method: Thermal scanning probe lithography creates a nanoscale-confined formation volume for local QD synthesis.
Direct writing is used to position CsPbI3 quantum dots at designed sites with spectral tunability.
The written emitters are coupled to photonic cavities to verify enhanced spontaneous emission.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports high-yield arrays of CsPbI3 single-photon emitters with narrow linewidths, room-temperature single-photon purity up to 98%, and measured spontaneous-emission enhancement in cavities.
watch_item: The approach depends on precise thermal scanning probe control and material stability, so scaling to large-area, high-throughput manufacturing may be challenging.
paper_title: Direct writing of individual quantum dots
